PDM and LSTM benchmark protocol

Source: benchmark-protocol.md

Version 0.3, 2026-11-02. Decisions closed; three facts to confirm before sign-off (section 12).

This protocol fixes how PDM and the LSTM models are compared before anyone sees a test result. Its purpose is simple: if the comparison is challenged, the answer is this document, dated and agreed in advance. It takes effect when an Owner is named and a Steward signs it off. No test period is scored before then.

1. Principle

Both models get the same data, the same periods and a stated, comparable search effort. Both are scored by the same code on the same masked observations. A basin enters or leaves the comparison for data reasons decided in advance, never because of its result.

The comparison is in simulation mode. Neither model sees observed flow at run time: PDM’s updating and state correction are off, and the LSTM takes no lagged discharge input. Forecast skill with assimilation is a different question and is outside this protocol.

2. Phases

Phase Data Step Purpose
1 CAMELS-GB (Coxon et al., 2020) Daily Prove the protocol, the scoring code and both teams’ processes on open data, against a published benchmark
2 Environment Agency gauged catchments 15 minutes The operationally relevant comparison

Phase 1 copies the design of Lees et al. (2021), so that both teams can check their setup against published results: the retrained LSTM against the published LSTM, and PDM against the four FUSE conceptual models in that study. Phase 1 results do not change any phase 2 decision; phase 2 decisions still open (section 11) are closed and versioned before phase 2 data are scored.

3. Basins

Phase 1. The 669 CAMELS-GB catchments used by Lees et al. (2021), listed in an appendix. The 518 catchments with FUSE results in that study form a fixed subset for the comparison with the published conceptual models. No further exclusions are made, except a basin where a model cannot run for a data reason found before scoring, recorded with the reason.

Phase 2. Selection criteria, fixed now; the list follows before calibration starts:

  • at least 15 years of 15-minute flow;
  • no more than 10 per cent missing in any period;
  • no significant regulation or abstraction, from the hydrometric register’s flags;
  • catchment area from 10 to 1,000 km2;
  • a deliberate spread of baseflow index, so that both groundwater-dominated and flashy catchments are represented.

In both phases, no basin is removed after test results exist.

4. Data

  • Time step: daily in phase 1, as CAMELS-GB; 15 minutes, UTC, in phase 2.
  • Forcing: both models receive the same precipitation and PET series, in mm per interval, from the same source and processing chain. In phase 1 these are the CAMELS-GB series. Gaps are infilled once, by one method, before either model sees the data.
  • LSTM inputs: the dynamic forcings and static catchment attributes used by Lees et al. (2021), listed in an appendix. PDM uses precipitation, PET and catchment area only. This is a legitimate difference between a regional and a per-basin model, not a fairness breach, but it is stated in every report.
  • Observed flow: in m3/s, mean flow over each interval, matching PDM’s q_m3s. Missing observations stay missing and are never infilled for scoring.

5. Periods

Periods are chronological and do not overlap. The same dates apply to every basin and both models.

Period Phase 1 dates PDM use LSTM use
Warm-up The year before training Simulated, not scored Sequence look-back
Training As Lees et al. (2021) Calibration Weight training
Validation As Lees et al. (2021) Calibration Early stopping and hyperparameters
Test 1998 to 2008, as Lees et al. (2021) Scored once Scored once

PDM is calibrated on the training and validation years combined, so that both models see the same years before the test and neither sees more. Every run under this protocol, the pilot included, therefore holds no years back: each basin’s basin.yml sets wettest_years: 0. The one exception is the separate extrapolation run of section 10a. Because PDM then has no held-out years, its structure and calibration method are fixed in advance (section 6) and not chosen from results.

The test period is scored once, after both models are frozen. Any rerun after test results are known is reported as such, with the reason.

6. PDM configuration

  • Package: pdmS7 at a recorded commit, compiled engine, adaptive groundwater solver.
  • Structure: Pareto capacity, standard recharge, two-store surface cascade, cubic groundwater, no snow. The same structure for every basin.
  • Parameters and bounds: calibration_bounds() of that structure, from inst/calibration-bounds.csv at the recorded commit, with the search scales given there. Bounds are not changed after test results exist.
  • Calibration method and effort: fixed by the pilot below, before any test score exists.
  • Runs: calibrate_batch(), one calibration-log project per basin, seeds derived from the basin’s identifier.
  • Diagnostics recorded per basin: every start’s objective, convergence code, evaluation count and fitted parameters; parameters within 1 per cent of a bound; wall time. The calibration log holds all of these.

Pilot

  • Basins: 20 phase 1 basins, chosen to span the range of baseflow index, listed in an appendix before the pilot runs.
  • Data: calibrate on the training years only; score on the validation years. The test years are not used.
  • Settings compared: calibration of all parameters at once (objective 1 minus NSE) and staged calibration (calibrate_staged() with the default stages), each at 3, 5, 10 and 20 starts.
  • Rule: the chosen setting is the cheapest, in total objective evaluations, whose median validation NSE over the 20 basins is within 0.01 of the best setting’s. The pilot results and the choice are recorded before the final calibration runs.

The final run then applies the chosen setting to every basin, on training and validation years.

7. LSTM configuration

  • Architecture, inputs and loss: as Lees et al. (2021). If the team uses NeuralHydrology, the configuration file is archived with the results and fixes all three.
  • Hyperparameter search: on the validation years only, with the search space and number of trials recorded.
  • Seeds: 8, as in Lees et al. (2021).
  • Reported model: the ensemble mean of the 8 seeds, with the spread across seeds alongside. The median single seed is also reported, so that averaging, which smooths errors a single PDM run keeps, can be judged.
  • Output handling: negative predicted flows are set to zero before scoring, and the number of intervals affected is reported.

8. Search effort and compute

The two models search in different ways, so effort cannot be equalised exactly. It is reported instead: PDM starts and objective evaluations against LSTM seeds, trials and epochs, with core-hours or GPU-hours for each. A reader can then judge whether either model was under-resourced.

9. Metrics

All metrics are computed on the test period by pdm_scorecard() from pdmS7, for both models and the lower benchmark, using the same observation mask. One scoring function removes one class of argument.

Metric pdm_scorecard() name What it shows
NSE (headline) nse Overall fit, dominated by high flows
KGE (headline) kge Correlation, variability and bias together
KGE terms kge_r, kge_alpha, kge_beta Where a KGE shortfall comes from
NSE of log flows log_nse Low-flow behaviour
RMSE, RMSE of log flows rmse, log_rmse Error in flow units, and in low flows
Volume error volume_error, abs_volume_error Water balance
Peak error peak_error Size of the largest flow in the test period
Flow-duration signatures fdc_high, fdc_mid, fdc_low High-flow volume, mid-segment slope and low-flow volume biases (Yilmaz et al., 2008)
  • Log offset: 1 per cent of each basin’s mean observed flow over the training years, so that log scores weigh small and large rivers alike.
  • Lower benchmark: for each basin, the mean observed flow for each day of the year over the training years, scored in the same way (Seibert et al., 2018). A model is judged against this floor as well as against the other model.
  • Peak timing is not assessed at a daily step.

10. Comparison and reporting

  • Per basin: every metric for both models and the lower benchmark in one table, including basins where PDM wins.
  • Across basins: median and interquartile range of each metric, and cumulative distribution plots.
  • Paired comparison: per-basin differences, the count of basins each model wins on each metric, and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test as a descriptive summary, not a verdict.
  • Published reference (phase 1): on the 518-basin subset, PDM beside the published FUSE results and the retrained LSTM beside the published LSTM.
  • Diagnostics: PDM basins with parameters on a bound or no converged start are flagged, not dropped. Results are reported with and without them.
  • Strata, fixed now: baseflow index, catchment area and aridity, each in thirds with cut points from all phase 1 basins set before scoring; and region as reported by Lees et al. (2021). Any other split is labelled exploratory.

10a. Supporting evidence: extrapolation (PDM only)

The comparison above says how well each model reproduces the test period. It does not say how either does on floods larger than those it was fitted to, which is where calibrations most often fail. This section reports that for PDM alone, as supporting evidence. It is not part of the head-to-head comparison, asks nothing of the LSTM team, and its results do not enter section 10’s tables.

  • Run: a second calibrate_batch() over the same basins, with the setting fixed by the pilot, on the same training and validation years, but with wettest_years: 2. The two water years with the highest observed flow in those years are held back from calibration and scored once, after the candidate is fixed (Klemeš 1986, differential split-sample test).
  • Reported per basin: NSE and KGE over the held-back years; for each held year, the observed peak, the calibrated peak, and the range of peaks across the equally good parameter sets (within 0.02 NSE of the best, up to 50 sets).
  • Rating: where the gauging authority supplies the highest gauged flow, it is registered as highest_gauged_m3s, and held-back peaks above it are flagged. Flagged basins are reported with and without them. Where it is not known, the results say so.
  • Across basins: the distribution of peak error on the held years, and of the width of the peak range, by the strata of section 10.

The test period of section 5 is not used here, so this run cannot inform anything in section 10. An LSTM extrapolation test, with both models retrained without the wettest years, is left to phase 2 or later, by agreement.

11. Phase 2 decisions to close before phase 2

Period dates; the basin list; the forcing product; the LSTM architecture for 15-minute data; and whether the phase 1 pilot’s choice carries over or a phase 2 pilot is run. Each is closed and the protocol versioned before any phase 2 test score exists.

12. Facts to confirm before sign-off

These are not decisions; they are copied from Lees et al. (2021) and checked against the paper:

  1. the training, validation and test dates, to the day;
  2. the LSTM dynamic inputs and static attributes;
  3. the list of 669 catchments and the 518-catchment subset.

13. Reproducibility

Recorded with the results: package commit, R version, operating system, seeds, the frozen configuration for each basin, the LSTM code version, configuration and weights, and the scored series. The outputs are archived with this protocol.

14. Agreement and changes

The protocol is recorded in a calibration-log project: an Owner is named when the project starts, each version is registered with its checksum, and a Steward signs it off. Calibration projects run under it cite the version they follow. Each change is versioned with its date and reason. A change made after any test result is known is reported in the results, with the comparison under the original protocol where possible.

References

  • Coxon, G. et al. (2020). CAMELS-GB: hydrometeorological time series and landscape attributes for 671 catchments in Great Britain. Earth System Science Data, 12, 2459–2483.
  • Klemeš, V. (1986). Operational testing of hydrological simulation models. Hydrological Sciences Journal, 31, 13–24.
  • Lees, T. et al. (2021). Benchmarking data-driven rainfall–runoff models in Great Britain: a comparison of long short-term memory (LSTM)-based models with four lumped conceptual models. Hydrology and Earth System Sciences, 25, 5517–5534.
  • Seibert, J. et al. (2018). Upper and lower benchmarks in hydrological modelling. Hydrological Processes, 32, 1120–1125.
  • Yilmaz, K. K. et al. (2008). A process-based diagnostic evaluation of a hydrologic model. Water Resources Research, 44, W09417.
